title: Generative AI Literacy Training Improves Intelligence Analysts' Discrimination of Real and AI-Generated Images
summary: Across social and online platforms, people are increasingly exposed to AI-generated images. As a consequence, the task of distinguishing AI-generated from authentic images is becoming a central challenge for information ecosystems. While humans perform better than chance, accuracy falls short of many operational needs. Initial evidence shows that visually oriented training can improve deepfake detection but does not improve participants' ability to identify real images as real. Here, we investigate the efficacy of a brief training intervention for intelligence analysts employed by the United States government in 2024. We conducted a counterbalanced within-subject randomized experiment in which we showed participants real and AI-generated images varying in pose complexity and scene context and asked them whether each image was real or AI-generated, both before and after an expert delivered a 30-minute training that pointed out patterns in seven real and 50 AI-generated images. We collected 2,544 image-level judgments from 32 intelligence analysts. We find training increased overall accuracy by 9 percentage points (95% CI: [2.7, 15.4]) from a baseline of 72%. We find the improvement is driven by a 14.2 percentage point increase in accuracy for real images (95% CI: [0.7, 27.7]). Through a careful experimental setup that curated matched pairs of real and AI-generated images across pose complexity categories, we reveal how these trainings influence people with different levels of digital forensics and generative AI experience and identify the kind of image-based content where this training intervention appears to be most effective. Ultimately, these results provide causal evidence that a brief, structured training can improve human judgment across a diverse array of real and AI-generated images, informing organizational responses to AI-generated visual misinformation.

title: GPTNT: Benchmarking Real-Time Collaboration Between Multimodal Agents on Keep Talking And Nobody Explodes
comments: Project website and code at https://gptnt.github.io
summary: Multimodal models are increasingly deployed to solve tasks collaboratively with humans or other artificial agents. Existing benchmarks show that these models possess many of the required component capabilities, but the conditions that coincide in collaboration, including time pressure, information asymmetry, and imperfect communication, are usually studied in isolation. We introduce GPTNT, a benchmark built on the cooperative video game Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes, in which two agents must coordinate to defuse procedurally generated bomb puzzles against a live countdown. One agent can see and manipulate the bomb but does not have the defusal instructions; the other has the instructions but cannot see or manipulate the bomb. Neither agent can succeed alone: success requires effective and efficient communication. Unlike turn-based proxies, GPTNT requires agents to act asynchronously and communicate in real time. GPTNT is designed to separate collaboration from reliance on memorized solutions: the instruction manual, the partner, or both can be withheld to isolate what a model derives in the moment from what it already knows. We show that GPTNT poses a substantial challenge for state-of-the-art systems: none of the closed- or open-source models we test defuses a single bomb in real time, a bar that human players clear. Through controlled experiments, we identify critical weaknesses in state tracking, efficient action under time pressure, ambiguity handling, and error recovery. We release GPTNT as a benchmark for collaborative performance that current evaluations leave unmeasured. Because it runs on the real game, GPTNT benefits from procedural generation and inherits a living modding community, allowing the benchmark to evolve as models improve rather than being solved once and retired.
comment: Project website and code at https://gptnt.github.io

title: CLEAR-MoE: Shared-Basis Expert Extraction from Frozen Vision Transformers via Calibration-Driven Layer Selection
summary: We present CLEAR-MoE, a four-phase post-training pipeline that converts a frozen pretrained Vision Transformer (ViT) into a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model without updating backbone weights. The pipeline (i) scores feed-forward network (FFN) layers by sparsity, clusterability, and output sensitivity; (ii) decomposes selected layers into a shared low-rank SVD basis and per-cluster residual experts using k-means clustering; (iii) trains lightweight routers supervised by cluster labels; and (iv) dispatches tokens through pluggable CUDA backends. On Imagenette with DeiT-Small, CLEAR-MoE retains 99.9% of the dense model's accuracy (86.70 +/- 0.02% versus 86.73%). Extensive ablation studies reveal a consistent empirical finding: the shared SVD basis is the primary factor responsible for preserving accuracy. Random routing, learned routing, and three different router architectures produce nearly identical performance, with accuracy varying by at most 0.06 percentage points (86.62%-86.68%). Accuracy also remains stable across different SVD ranks, expert counts (2-8), calibration set sizes (50-500), and random seeds. This behavior generalizes across five ViT backbones (DeiT-Tiny, DeiT-Small, DeiT-Base, ViT-Small, and ViT-Base), covering models from 5.7M to 86.6M parameters, with accuracy differences <= 0.10 percentage points from their dense counterparts. On a GTX 960 GPU, routing and scatter-gather overhead make the CLEAR-MoE FFN 1.3-1.7x slower than the dense implementation. A dispatch microbenchmark further shows that routing is an order of magnitude more memory-bound than expert matrix multiplications, identifying fused dispatch kernels as a promising direction for future optimization.

title: Drag, Infer, Reproject: Grounding LLMs through Spatial Interaction for Image Clustering
summary: Dimension reduction and semantic interaction support image clustering by making similarity structure visible and manipulable. Existing semantic interaction methods encode users' clustering criterion (a user-interpretable semantic dimension, e.g., action, location, or mood) from direct manipulation to steer reprojection, giving users direct control over the resulting layout. Yet they typically depend on learned embeddings or a predefined criterion. In practice, users' clustering criterion often emerges gradually and becomes refined through interaction rather than being fully clear at the outset. In this work, we present CriterionSI (Criterion-guided Semantic Interaction), a method that translates incremental drag interactions into criterion-guided reprojection. CriterionSI uses large language models to infer and refine the clustering criterion from sequential user drags, while grounding semantic interpretation in human-provided feedback rather than fixed prior assumptions. CriterionSI combines the inferred criterion with local drags to guide global reprojection. The simulation-based evaluation and usage scenario demonstrate that CriterionSI can discover and refine the target criterion from sequential interactions and progressively produce criterion-aligned clustering layouts. Our code and data are available at: https://github.com/4C79/CriterionSI.

title: A Trainable-by-Parts Operator Learning Framework: Bridging DeepONet and Karhunen-Loeve Expansions for Large-Scale Applications
summary: Training operator-learning models for large-scale problems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs) is challenging due to the curse of dimensionality, memory constraints, and limited training data. These challenges arise in many scientific and engineering applications, including subsurface flow, climate modeling, and geological carbon storage (GCS). In this work, we propose a scalable operator-learning framework based on the Karhunen-Loeve Deep Neural Network (KL-DNN) and demonstrate its performance for modeling GCS. The model is trained on a dataset comprising 100 samples of large-scale simulations in a three-dimensional domain with 1.7 million cells and 50 time steps. The KL-DNN method constructs latent spaces using low-rank singular value decomposition of static properties and a nested Karhunen-Loeve expansion for dynamic pressure fields, enabling full-resolution predictions without subsampling or spatial coarsening. The KL-DNN model achieves an average root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.1 psi for pressure (0.04% relative error with respect to the average pressure in the domain) and RMSE of 0.0146 for CO2 saturation (5% relative error with respect to the average saturation inside the plume). The model requires 20 minutes of training on a single GPU, representing a 19% reduction in the pressure errors, 7% reduction in the saturation error, and a two-order-of-magnitude speedup compared to DeepONet trained on the same dataset. These results, along with inference time of less than one minute, establish the proposed model as a practical and accurate solution for large-scale PDE problems, enabling rapid uncertainty quantification, history matching, and real-time decision support.

title: Detecting Clinical Hallucinations in LVLMs via Counterfactual Visual Grounding Uncertainty
summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) are increasingly used for clinical image understanding, yet they remain vulnerable to \emph{hallucinations}--producing textual findings or attributes not supported by the image. We present a vision-traceable hallucination detection framework that audits arbitrary LVLM responses via visual evidence grounding, requiring neither modification nor internal access to the hidden states of LVLMs. Given an LVLM response, we extract visually verifiable entities and use a medical-domain-adapted Qwen-VL grounding verifier to localize each entity on the input image. To enhance the robustness of our detection method, we introduce a counterfactual entity perturbation method and estimate visual evidence uncertainty by contrasting factual and counterfactual grounding results. Specifically, we compute an entity-level uncertainty score from the positive confidence, counterfactual confidence, and their grounding overlap for binary hallucination decision-making. Experiments on multiple medical imaging modalities and LVLM backbones demonstrate that our method consistently improves hallucination detection performance over recent baselines, while providing interpretable localization evidence and strong cross-model transferability. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Agentic-CliniAI/CounterVHD.

title: Developmental Trajectories of Situation Modeling and Mentalizing in Transformer Language Models
comments: Non-archival submission to the First Workshop on Computational Developmental Linguistics
summary: Recent work suggests that Large Language Models (LLMs) are sensitive to the belief states of agents described by text, as measured by the false belief task (FBT), yet persistent concerns of construct validity remain. We adopt a **developmental perspective**, tracing the pattern of mental state reasoning behavior -- and likely **preconditions** for this behavior -- across multiple training stages in the Olmo2 and Pythia language model suites. We find that above-chance FBT performance depends both on model size and sufficient training volume, emerges relatively late in pretraining, and is most improved by post-training interventions (SFT, DPO) in the condition most diagnostic of mentalizing (False Belief, Implicit). However, FBT performance is fragile: consistent with past work, the use of non-factive verbs (e.g., thinks) increases false belief attributions even in the True Belief condition. To contextualize these findings, we track the emergence of **situation modeling**: the ability to report on basic factual properties of a described scene. Situation modeling accuracy generally precedes and exceeds FBT accuracy, yet situational representations also prove surprisingly incoherent in certain respects: when asked about the knowledge states of the Antagonist agent -- who always knows the item's true location -- Olmo2 13b is consistently influenced both by the Target agent's knowledge state and the presence of non-factive verbs. Together, these results suggest that larger, sufficiently trained models build partially coherent situation models in a developmentally appropriate sequence, yet display surprising fragility -- highlighting the value of developmental and stress-testing approaches for evaluating LLM capabilities.
comment: Non-archival submission to the First Workshop on Computational Developmental Linguistics

title: A Gravitational Interpretation of Fine-Tuning Reversion
summary: Fine-tuning on harmless data can partially undo behaviors acquired earlier in training. Safety can erode under benign post-alignment updates, unlearned capabilities can re-emerge, latent traits can transfer through apparently unrelated supervision, and related post-alignment fragility appears in other generative settings. We argue these phenomena are usefully viewed through a common training-history lens. Our hypothesis is geometric: large early training phases create dominant behavioral manifolds, while later alignment or specialization phases are shallower displacements from them. Subsequent fine-tuning can therefore inherit a persistent reversion component pointing back toward a witness of the dominant manifold. We call this the gravitational interpretation of fine-tuning reversion. Across our main settings, representational drift rapidly acquires a component along a history-defined reversion direction (v_rev). In our main track, alignment with v_rev rises from cos = 0.429 +/- 0.052 after the first update to 0.647 +/- 0.021 by step 20. Across 24 run-step pairs, every observed alignment exceeds the p99 of an isotropic activation-space null. We demonstrate that selectively blocking motion along v_rev changes the final alignment at T=100 from 0.648 +/- 0.009 to -0.211 +/- 0.021 and reduces harmfulness from 19.0% +/- 4.0% to 8.5% +/- 1.5% with little task cost. These results support v_rev as a causally relevant mediator of early post-alignment reversion in our setup. Importantly, we do not claim that v_rev is the unique safety direction, nor that the dominant manifold is directly observed; rather, we identify a robust, history-defined direction that explains and partially controls early reversion dynamics.

title: A French OSCE Dialogue Dataset and Controllable Virtual Patient System for Clinical Training
summary: The clinical and communication skills of medical students are commonly assessed through Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs), which consist of brief scenario-driven simulations of doctor-patient interactions. However, training is often limited by the low availability of human standardized patients, motivating the development of realistic virtual patients (VPs). To address this gap, we introduce a French OSCE dialogue dataset comprising 240 student-patient training interactions. We build upon it a controllable LLM-based pipeline to generate synthetic OSCE dialogues. The pipeline integrates modular components, such as retrieval-based grounding and a reflection loop, to ensure patient fidelity, coherence, and realism. Additionally, we propose a multi-level evaluation framework assessing patient simulation quality, student performance, and linguistic quality, using an LLM-as-a-Judge approach. Experiments suggest that controllability modules generally improve patient fidelity and student evaluation consistency. Finally, we implement an interactive prototype in which students can practice with a VP and receive automatic feedback.

title: The Speedup Paradox: Rethinking Inference Speed-Quality Trade-off in Embodied Tasks
summary: Embodied foundation models have recently been widely used to improve robot generalization and task success rates. Previous works apply lossy efficient-inference techniques such as quantization, pruning, and asynchronous inference, accepting small action quality degradation in exchange for lower per-step computation cost and inter-action latency. However, unlike traditional static ML tasks, embodied tasks involve repeated interaction with the environment, and task-level performance is determined not only by per-step cost, but also by closed-loop effects unique to embodied execution, which remain insufficiently characterized in current efficient-inference studies. In this work, we propose TISED (\underline{T}ask-level \underline{I}nference \underline{S}peedup \underline{E}ffect \underline{D}ecomposition), an analytical framework that unifies diverse lossy inference optimization techniques and decomposes their effects on static and dynamic tasks, and uncovers some paradoxical effects on task-level performance: (1) on \textit{static tasks}, optimization sometimes can lengthen end-to-end per-task completion time even as per-step latency drops; (2) on \textit{dynamic tasks}, moderate lossy optimization can raise task success rate even above the baseline; and (3) the monotonicity and sweet-spot location of both effects can shift with hardware configuration. Together, our findings provide a new perspective on adapting inference optimization techniques to embodied tasks.

title: Density Functions and Random Number Generators of $α$-Stable Distributions
summary: Heavy-tailed distributions are increasingly found to better fit empirical data in engineering, finance, physics, network science, and related fields. Among them, $α$-stable distributions play a central role being limiting laws in the generalized central limit theorem: they are expected to be exceptionally good models whenever sums of multiple independent heavy-tailed sources are at play. Despite their theoretical importance, their practical use remains challenging: $α$-stable probability densities generally do not have closed-form expressions, and numerical evaluation and random variate generation can be difficult, especially in the multivariate setting. This paper presents AUB-HTP, a Python package for numerical computation and simulation of $α$-stable distributions. The package provides scalar density evaluation using several complementary methods, including Zolotarev-type integral representations, series formulas, and numerical inversion of characteristic functions. It also provides random variate generation for scalar and multivariate $α$-stable distributions, with support for flexible spectral measures through LePage series representations. Numerical experiments demonstrate that AUB-HTP improves the accuracy, stability, and parameter coverage of existing tools for scalar density computation, while adding new capabilities for multivariate simulation. The package is designed to support reproducible computational work involving heavy-tailed models across a broad range of scientific applications.

AI.title_translation: α-稳定分布的密度函数和随机数生成器
AI.tldr: 本文介绍了AUB-HTP，一个Python包，用于准确、稳定地计算和模拟α-稳定分布的密度函数和随机数，解决了现有工具的局限性，并增加了多元模拟能力。
AI.motivation: 重尾分布在工程、金融、物理、网络科学等领域越来越普遍，而α-稳定分布作为广义中心极限定理的极限分布，在多独立重尾源求和的场景中是理想模型。然而，其概率密度函数通常没有封闭形式，数值评估和随机变量生成（尤其是在多元情况下）面临挑战，限制了其实际应用。
AI.method: 论文介绍了AUB-HTP，一个Python包，用于α-稳定分布的数值计算和模拟。它通过Zolotarev型积分表示、级数公式和特征函数的数值反演等多种互补方法提供标量密度评估。它还通过LePage级数表示为标量和多元α-稳定分布提供随机变量生成，支持灵活的谱测度。
AI.result: 数值实验表明，AUB-HTP提高了现有工具在标量密度计算方面的准确性、稳定性及参数覆盖范围，同时增加了多元模拟的新功能。
AI.conclusion: AUB-HTP包旨在支持在广泛科学应用中涉及重尾模型的可重复计算工作。
AI.translation: 重尾分布在工程、金融、物理、网络科学及相关领域中被发现能更好地拟合经验数据。其中，α-稳定分布作为广义中心极限定理的极限分布，扮演着核心角色：当多个独立的重尾源的总和起作用时，它们有望成为异常优秀的模型。尽管它们具有理论重要性，但其实际应用仍然充满挑战：α-稳定概率密度通常没有封闭形式的表达式，数值评估和随机变量生成可能很困难，尤其是在多元设置中。本文介绍了AUB-HTP，一个用于α-稳定分布数值计算和模拟的Python包。该包使用几种互补方法提供标量密度评估，包括Zolotarev型积分表示、级数公式和特征函数的数值反演。它还为标量和多元α-稳定分布提供随机变量生成，并通过LePage级数表示支持灵活的谱测度。数值实验表明，AUB-HTP提高了现有工具在标量密度计算方面的准确性、稳定性及参数覆盖范围，同时增加了多元模拟的新功能。该包旨在支持在广泛科学应用中涉及重尾模型的可重复计算工作。
AI.summary: 本文介绍并发布了AUB-HTP，一个用Python实现的开源软件包，旨在解决α-稳定分布在数值计算和随机数生成方面的挑战。α-稳定分布在多种科学领域中作为重尾数据的理想模型，但因其概率密度缺乏封闭形式而难以应用。AUB-HTP通过集成多种数值方法，包括Zolotarev型积分、级数公式和特征函数反演，实现了标量密度函数的准确评估，并通过LePage级数表示支持了标量及多元α-稳定分布的随机数生成。实验结果验证了AUB-HTP在准确性、稳定性、参数覆盖方面优于现有工具，并提供了新的多元模拟能力，从而促进了重尾模型在科学研究中的可重复应用。
AI.keywords: α-稳定分布, 重尾分布, 随机数生成, 密度函数, Python包
AI.comments: 这项工作通过提供一个高效、准确且功能更全面的Python包AUB-HTP，显著降低了α-稳定分布在实际应用中的门槛。其创新之处在于整合了多种先进的数值计算方法，并首次提供了对多元α-稳定分布的有效模拟支持，这对于需要处理复杂重尾现象的研究者来说是一个重要的工具。该包的发布将有助于推动涉及重尾模型在工程、金融、物理等多个领域的应用和研究。

title: A Good Talk Does not Look Like a Summary, It Teaches You! Measuring Takeaways from Paper-to-Video Talks
summary: Automatically generated videos from scientific papers are increasingly used for education and research dissemination. However, existing evaluation metrics mainly measure visual quality or whether key points from the paper appear in the video without assessing whether the video actually helps viewers understand the ideas. We introduce EffectivePresentationScorer, a framework for evaluating the instructional quality of scientific presentation videos. It checks whether a video explains the main ideas clearly, introduces needed background concepts, and connects technical details to the main contribution of the paper. When we apply EffectivePresentationScorer to the existing paper-to-video generation systems, we find that generated videos mention the correct topics and follow the structure of the paper but fail to explain prerequisite concepts or clarify why the method works. These failures are often ignored by existing video evaluation metrics, which focus on content presence rather than explanatory quality.

AI.title_translation: 好的演讲不像摘要，它会教你东西！衡量论文转视频演讲的收获
AI.tldr: 现有论文转视频的评估指标未能衡量教学质量。本文提出了EffectivePresentationScorer框架，评估视频是否真正帮助观众理解。研究发现，现有系统虽能覆盖主题和结构，但在解释先决概念和方法原理方面表现不足。
AI.motivation: 现有的从科学论文自动生成的视频评估指标主要衡量视觉质量或关键点是否出现，但未能评估视频是否真正帮助观众理解思想。
AI.method: 本文引入了EffectivePresentationScorer框架，用于评估科学演示视频的教学质量。该框架检查视频是否清晰解释主要思想、引入所需背景概念，并将技术细节与论文主要贡献联系起来。
AI.result: 应用EffectivePresentationScorer于现有论文转视频生成系统后发现，生成的视频虽提及正确主题并遵循论文结构，但未能解释先决概念或阐明方法为何有效。这些缺陷常被现有关注内容存在而非解释质量的视频评估指标所忽略。
AI.conclusion: 现有的论文转视频生成系统在内容呈现和结构方面表现良好，但在解释先决知识和方法原理的教学质量方面存在明显不足，而这些不足是现有评估指标未能有效捕捉的。
AI.translation: 从科学论文自动生成的视频越来越多地用于教育和研究传播。然而，现有的评估指标主要衡量视觉质量或论文中的关键点是否出现在视频中，而没有评估视频是否真正帮助观众理解这些思想。我们引入了EffectivePresentationScorer，一个用于评估科学演示视频教学质量的框架。它检查视频是否清晰地解释了主要思想，介绍了所需的背景概念，并将技术细节与论文的主要贡献联系起来。当我们把EffectivePresentationScorer应用于现有的论文转视频生成系统时，我们发现生成的视频提及了正确的主题并遵循了论文的结构，但未能解释先决概念或阐明方法为何有效。这些失败常常被现有的视频评估指标所忽略，因为它们关注的是内容的存在而非解释质量。
AI.summary: 鉴于现有评估指标无法衡量论文转视频的教学质量，本文提出了EffectivePresentationScorer框架。该框架通过检查视频对核心思想的解释、背景概念的引入以及技术细节与贡献的关联来评估教学效果。应用该框架后发现，尽管现有系统能覆盖主题并遵循结构，但在解释先决条件和方法原理方面存在不足，这表明现有评估方法侧重内容存在而非解释质量的局限性。
AI.keywords: 教学质量, 论文转视频, 评估框架, 科学演示, 知识理解
AI.comments: 这篇论文强调了从科学论文自动生成视频时，教学质量而非仅仅内容覆盖的重要性，填补了现有评估指标的空白。EffectivePresentationScorer的引入对于提升教育和研究传播视频的有效性具有重要意义，促使未来的生成系统更加注重知识的传递和理解。

title: CMSL: Constructive Multi-Sequence Learning for Recommendation Systems
summary: Sequence learning has emerged as the promising paradigm in recommendation systems, surpassing traditional Deep Learning Recommendation Models (DLRM) by capturing the temporal nuances of user behavior. However, current state-of-the-art architectures operate under a limiting analogy: they treat user history as a monolithic chronological sequence like a sentence in a Large Language Model (LLM). We observe a fundamental divergence between natural language and recommendation data: unlike the linear, logical flow of text, user history is inherently multi-faceted. A user's journey is a fragmented reflection of diverse interests, resulting in much weaker coherence between items than is found in LLM training data. This lack of structural unity leads to context pollution. In single-sequence modeling, unrelated behaviors compete for the same attention budget. This "noisy" signal dilutes the model's focus, effectively capping its ability to discern high-intent patterns from background activity. To address this, we propose Constructive Multi-Sequence Learning (CMSL), a paradigm shift from passive sequence ingestion to active "context engineering" that constructs multiple coherent sequences in latent space. CMSL leverages a learnable Sequence Construction Module to disentangle user history into "pure" thematic strands, followed by a linear attention mechanism to efficiently model these strands at scale. CMSL has been deployed across ranking and retrieval tasks and across four major surfaces at Meta.

AI.title_translation: CMSL: 推荐系统中的建构式多序列学习
AI.tldr: 现有推荐系统序列模型将用户历史视为单一序列，导致上下文污染。CMSL通过构建多个连贯的潜在序列来解决此问题，并在Meta部署。
AI.motivation: 现有推荐系统中的序列学习模型将用户历史视为单一的、整体的按时间顺序排列的序列，类似于大型语言模型（LLM）中的句子。然而，用户历史是多方面的，项目之间的连贯性较弱，导致“上下文污染”，即不相关的行为争夺相同的注意力预算，稀释了模型识别高意图模式的能力。
AI.method: 本文提出了建构式多序列学习（CMSL），这是一种从被动序列摄取到主动“上下文工程”的范式转变。CMSL利用一个可学习的序列构建模块将用户历史解构为“纯粹的”主题线索，然后利用线性注意力机制在大规模上高效地建模这些线索，从而在潜在空间中构建多个连贯的序列。
AI.result: CMSL已在Meta的排名和检索任务以及四个主要界面中部署。
AI.conclusion: CMSL通过主动的“上下文工程”构建多个连贯序列，有效解决了推荐系统中单一序列建模的上下文污染问题，提高了模型识别用户高意图模式的能力，证明了其在实际应用中的有效性。
AI.translation: 序列学习已成为推荐系统中有前景的范式，通过捕捉用户行为的时间细微差别超越了传统的深度学习推荐模型（DLRM）。然而，当前最先进的架构在一个限制性类比下运行：它们将用户历史视为一个单一的按时间顺序排列的序列，就像大型语言模型（LLM）中的一个句子。我们观察到自然语言和推荐数据之间存在根本性差异：与文本的线性、逻辑流不同，用户历史本质上是多方面的。用户的旅程是不同兴趣的碎片化反映，导致项目之间的连贯性远低于LLM训练数据中的连贯性。这种结构统一性的缺乏导致了上下文污染。在单一序列建模中，不相关的行为争夺相同的注意力预算。这种“嘈杂的”信号稀释了模型的焦点，有效地限制了其从背景活动中识别高意图模式的能力。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了建构式多序列学习（CMSL），这是一种从被动序列摄取到主动“上下文工程”的范式转变，它在潜在空间中构建多个连贯的序列。CMSL利用一个可学习的序列构建模块将用户历史解构为“纯粹的”主题线索，然后利用线性注意力机制大规模高效地建模这些线索。CMSL已在Meta的排名和检索任务以及四个主要界面中部署。
AI.summary: 本文提出了建构式多序列学习（CMSL），旨在解决现有推荐系统序列模型中将用户历史视为单一序列导致的上下文污染问题。CMSL通过一个可学习的序列构建模块将用户历史解构为多个主题线索，并在潜在空间中构建连贯序列，再通过线性注意力机制进行高效建模。该方法已在Meta的实际排名和检索任务中成功部署。
AI.keywords: 推荐系统, 序列学习, 上下文污染, 多序列学习, CMSL
AI.comments: CMSL的创新之处在于其“上下文工程”范式，它通过主动构建多序列来解决传统单一序列模型中的上下文污染和噪声信号问题。这种方法认识到用户行为的复杂性和多面性，而非简单地将其视为线性序列，这对于提高推荐系统的准确性和效率具有重要意义。在大型科技公司Meta的实际部署也证明了其实用性和有效性。

title: MammoFlow: Multiview Mammogram Synthesis with Anatomically Consistent Flow Matching
summary: Multiview mammography relies on paired craniocaudal (CC) and mediolateral oblique (MLO) views to provide complementary projections of a 3D breast volume, enabling precise anomaly localization. However, acquiring high-quality, balanced datasets remains challenging for deep learning applications. We propose a novel method to synthesize multiview mammograms by leveraging the inherent geometric relationship between CC and MLO views. To enforce an implicit 3D consistency prior during generation, we develop an alignment module that searches a 2D affine transformation subspace to establish optimal anatomical correspondence. Leveraging this alignment, we introduce a pixel-space self-consistency loss based on the Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) between the 1D anteroposterior (AP) axis tissue distributions of the generated images. Integrated into a pretrained flow matching model, MammoFlow forces synthesized pairs to share physically plausible tissue distributions from the chest wall to the nipple. To our knowledge, this is the first work to guide multiview mammogram generation using implicit geometric tissue correspondence. Our method demonstrates superior image quality, passes expert radiologist evaluation, and generates physically consistent pairs that improve downstream classification AUC by 5%. Code is available at https://github.com/XYPB/MammoFlow

AI.title_translation: MammoFlow：基于解剖学一致流匹配的多视图乳腺X线图像合成
AI.tldr: MammoFlow提出了一种新方法，通过利用CC和MLO视图间的几何关系，并引入对齐模块和基于EMD的像素空间自一致性损失，合成具有解剖学一致性的多视图乳腺X线图像，提升了图像质量和下游分类性能。
AI.motivation: 深度学习应用中，获取高质量、平衡的多视图乳腺X线图像数据集具有挑战性，而多视图乳腺X线图像对于精确的异常定位至关重要。
AI.method: 本文提出MammoFlow，通过利用头尾位（CC）和内外侧斜位（MLO）视图固有的几何关系来合成多视图乳腺X线图像。方法包括开发一个对齐模块，搜索2D仿射变换子空间以建立最佳解剖对应关系；在此基础上，引入了基于生成图像的1D前后轴组织分布之间地球移动距离（EMD）的像素空间自一致性损失。MammoFlow将这些集成到一个预训练的流匹配模型中，强制合成的图像对共享物理上合理的组织分布。
AI.result: 该方法展示了卓越的图像质量，通过了专家放射科医生的评估，并生成了物理上一致的图像对，将下游分类的AUC提高了5%。
AI.conclusion: MammoFlow是首个利用隐式几何组织对应关系指导多视图乳腺X线图像生成的工作，能够合成高质量、解剖学一致的图像，并显著改善下游分类任务的性能。
AI.translation: 多视图乳腺X线摄影依赖于成对的头尾位 (CC) 和内外侧斜位 (MLO) 视图，以提供 3D 乳房体积的互补投影，从而实现精确的异常定位。然而，对于深度学习应用而言，获取高质量、平衡的数据集仍然具有挑战性。我们提出了一种新颖的方法，通过利用 CC 和 MLO 视图之间固有的几何关系来合成多视图乳腺X线图像。为了在生成过程中强制执行隐式 3D 一致性先验，我们开发了一个对齐模块，该模块搜索 2D 仿射变换子空间以建立最佳解剖对应关系。利用这种对齐，我们引入了一种基于生成图像的 1D 前后 (AP) 轴组织分布之间地球移动距离 (EMD) 的像素空间自一致性损失。MammoFlow 集成到一个预训练的流匹配模型中，强制合成的图像对共享从胸壁到乳头的物理上合理的组织分布。据我们所知，这是首个利用隐式几何组织对应关系指导多视图乳腺X线图像生成的工作。我们的方法展示了卓越的图像质量，通过了专家放射科医生的评估，并生成了物理上一致的图像对，将下游分类的 AUC 提高了 5%。代码可在 https://github.com/XYPB/MammoFlow 获取。
AI.summary: 本文提出MammoFlow，一个用于合成多视图乳腺X线图像的新方法，旨在解决深度学习中高质量数据集获取的挑战。该方法通过一个对齐模块建立CC和MLO视图间的解剖对应，并引入基于EMD的像素空间自一致性损失，集成到流匹配模型中，以确保生成图像的物理一致性。MammoFlow在图像质量和专家评估中表现出色，并能将下游分类任务的AUC提高5%。
AI.keywords: 乳腺X线图像合成, 多视图, 流匹配, 几何对应, 数据增强
AI.comments: MammoFlow的创新在于首次利用隐式几何组织对应关系来指导多视图乳腺X线图像生成，通过对齐模块和EMD损失确保了合成图像的解剖学和物理一致性。这对于解决医学图像领域数据稀缺问题具有重要意义，并能有效提升下游任务的性能。

title: Legal Domain Adaptation of Modern BERT Models
comments: To appear in Proceedings of the 21st International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Law (ICAIL 2026), June 9-12, 2026, Singapore
summary: We investigate domain adaptation of modern BERT models in the legal domain. We further pre-train ModernBERT on all US court opinions using the masked language modeling objective. Although ModernBERT has been trained on roughly 500x more data than original BERT, we still find that this model benefits from further pre-training and domain adaptation in the legal domain: we report significant improvements compared to vanilla ModernBERT on all datasets connected to US court opinions. We find gains similar to those reported in early work on domain adaptation of BERT-like models. However, from scratch pre-training does not match the performance of further pre-training an existing ModernBERT checkpoint in our experiments. The resulting models are capable of processing sequences up to 8,192 tokens, and can be used to compute meaningful embeddings of legal passages, or could quickly rerank hundreds of legal passages for a given search query. We release all model checkpoints publicly.
comment: To appear in Proceedings of the 21st International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Law (ICAIL 2026), June 9-12, 2026, Singapore

AI.title_translation: 现代BERT模型在法律领域的领域适应
AI.tldr: 该研究探讨了现代BERT模型在法律领域的领域适应，发现即使是经过大量数据训练的ModernBERT，在法律领域进行进一步预训练也能显著提升性能，并且进一步预训练现有检查点比从头开始训练更有效。
AI.motivation: 研究现代大型BERT模型是否仍在特定领域（如法律领域）受益于领域适应，并提升其在法律任务上的性能。
AI.method: 1. 使用掩码语言建模目标，在所有美国法院意见书上对ModernBERT进行进一步预训练。2. 将其性能与原始ModernBERT在法律数据集上进行比较。3. 比较进一步预训练现有检查点和从头开始预训练的性能。
AI.result: 1. 与原始ModernBERT相比，在所有与美国法院意见书相关的数据集上报告了显著的性能改进。2. 获得的收益与早期关于BERT类模型领域适应工作的报告相似。3. 进一步预训练现有ModernBERT检查点比从头开始预训练表现更好。4. 最终模型能够处理长达8,192个token的序列。5. 模型可用于计算法律段落的有意义的嵌入，或快速重新排序法律段落。
AI.conclusion: 现代BERT模型，即使在经过大量初始训练后，仍然能通过在特定领域数据（如法律文本）上进行进一步预训练而显著受益于领域适应。进一步预训练现有检查点比从头开始预训练更有效。
AI.translation: 我们研究了现代BERT模型在法律领域的领域适应。我们使用掩码语言建模目标，在所有美国法院意见书上对ModernBERT进行了进一步预训练。尽管ModernBERT的训练数据量大约是原始BERT的500倍，但我们仍然发现该模型在法律领域的进一步预训练和领域适应中受益：与香草ModernBERT相比，我们在所有与美国法院意见书相关的数据集上报告了显著的改进。我们发现的收益与早期关于BERT类模型领域适应工作的报告相似。然而，在我们的实验中，从头开始预训练无法匹配进一步预训练现有ModernBERT检查点的性能。由此产生的模型能够处理长达8,192个token的序列，可用于计算法律段落的有意义的嵌入，或者可以快速重新排序给定搜索查询的数百个法律段落。我们公开发布所有模型检查点。
AI.summary: 本文研究了现代BERT模型在法律领域的领域适应。通过使用掩码语言建模目标，在所有美国法院意见书上对ModernBERT进行进一步预训练，作者证明了即使ModernBERT已经拥有大量的训练数据，其在法律数据集上的性能仍比原始版本有显著提升。研究发现，进一步预训练现有检查点比从头开始训练更有效。最终模型支持长达8,192个token的序列，可用于法律文本嵌入和重新排序。
AI.keywords: 法律领域适应, BERT, ModernBERT, 预训练, 掩码语言建模
AI.comments: 这篇论文强调了即使对于像ModernBERT这样非常大的预训练语言模型，领域适应仍然具有重要意义。研究发现进一步预训练现有模型优于从头开始训练，这为资源有限的研究提供了实用的见解。模型检查点的公开发布对法律自然语言处理社区是一个宝贵的贡献。

title: KoAT: Automatic Complexity and Termination Analysis of Integer Programs
summary: KoAT is a tool to automatically infer complexity bounds and prove termination of (possibly recursive) integer programs. To this end, KoAT implements an alternating modular inference of upper runtime and size bounds for program parts. In particular, KoAT uses a portfolio of different techniques to analyze subprograms. The power of our approach is demonstrated by an extensive experimental evaluation.

AI.title_translation: KoAT：整数程序的自动复杂度和终止性分析
AI.tldr: KoAT是一个工具，可以自动推断整数程序的复杂度界限并证明其终止性，它通过模块化推断和多种技术组合实现。
AI.motivation: 自动推断整数程序的复杂度和证明其终止性是重要的，因为这有助于理解和验证程序的行为。
AI.method: KoAT实现了对程序部分进行交替模块化推断，以获取运行时和大小的上限。它还使用了多种技术组合来分析子程序。
AI.result: 该方法的强大之处通过广泛的实验评估得到了证实。
AI.conclusion: KoAT能够有效地自动推断整数程序的复杂度和证明其终止性，并且其有效性已通过实验验证。
AI.translation: KoAT是一个用于自动推断（可能递归的）整数程序的复杂性界限并证明其终止性的工具。为此，KoAT实现了对程序部分进行交替模块化推断，以获得运行时和大小的上限。特别是，KoAT使用了一系列不同的技术来分析子程序。我们方法的强大之处通过广泛的实验评估得到了证明。
AI.summary: KoAT是一种自动化工具，旨在分析整数程序的复杂度和终止性。它通过对程序部分进行模块化推断，并结合多种分析技术，来确定程序的运行时和大小上限。该方法的有效性已通过实验评估得到验证。
AI.keywords: 复杂性分析, 终止性证明, 整数程序, 自动化工具, KoAT
AI.comments: 这篇论文介绍了一个实用的自动化工具KoAT，用于解决程序分析中的核心问题：复杂度和终止性。其模块化推理和技术组合的方法可能提高了分析的效率和准确性，对于软件验证和性能优化具有重要意义。

title: Who Plays Which Role When? Communication Role Dynamics for Peer Recognition and Team Performance Prediction
summary: Team roles offer an interpretable lens on collaboration, yet computational studies of roles often rely on domain-specific personas or data-driven clustering rather than theory-grounded taxonomies. We operationalize a taxonomy of eight communication roles grounded in education literature and annotate a corpus of 6,307 Slack messages from 55 students across 18 teams in a semester-long computer science course project. We evaluate whether LLMs can approximate expert labels, enabling scalable, taxonomy-driven role annotation. Using these role labels, we characterize role dynamics over teams' lifecycles, finding that different roles peak at different moments and that students enact a more diverse set of roles as projects progress. To evaluate the utility of our role constructs, we use them to predict peer recognition, outperforming lexical, conversational, and LLM-prompting baselines. To assess generalizability beyond the educational context, we apply the same role constructs to a public dataset (DeliData) to predict team performance improvement after deliberation, again exceeding prior performance.

AI.title_translation: 谁在何时扮演什么角色？用于同伴认可和团队绩效预测的沟通角色动态
AI.tldr: 研究基于教育文献的沟通角色分类法，用LLM标注Slack消息，发现角色动态可预测同伴认可和团队绩效。
AI.motivation: 现有的计算角色研究常依赖特定领域或数据驱动聚类，而非理论基础分类法，导致缺乏可解释性。本研究旨在通过理论基础的沟通角色分类法来解决这一问题。
AI.method: 操作化了基于教育文献的八种沟通角色分类法；标注了一个包含6,307条Slack消息的语料库；评估了大型语言模型（LLMs）近似专家标签的能力以实现可扩展的角色标注；利用角色标签描述团队生命周期中的角色动态；使用角色构建来预测同伴认可和团队绩效提升。
AI.result: 不同沟通角色在团队生命周期的不同时刻达到高峰；随着项目进展，学生扮演的角色更加多样化；沟通角色构建在预测同伴认可方面优于词汇、对话和LLM提示基线；沟通角色构建在预测团队审议后的绩效提升方面超越了现有表现，证明了其在教育背景之外的通用性。
AI.conclusion: 本研究成功操作化了理论基础的沟通角色分类法，并证明了其在预测同伴认可和团队绩效方面的有效性和通用性。
AI.translation: 团队角色为协作提供了一个可解释的视角，然而，对角色的计算研究往往依赖于特定领域的角色或数据驱动的聚类，而非以理论为基础的分类法。我们操作化了一个以教育文献为基础的八种沟通角色分类法，并标注了一个包含6,307条Slack消息的语料库，这些消息来自一个学期长的计算机科学课程项目中的18个团队的55名学生。我们评估了大型语言模型（LLMs）是否能近似专家标签，从而实现可扩展的、以分类法为驱动的角色标注。利用这些角色标签，我们描述了团队生命周期中的角色动态，发现不同的角色在不同时刻达到高峰，并且随着项目进展，学生扮演的角色更加多样化。为了评估我们角色构建的效用，我们使用它们来预测同伴认可，其表现优于词汇、对话和LLM提示基线。为了评估教育背景之外的通用性，我们将相同的角色构建应用于公共数据集（DeliData），以预测审议后的团队绩效提升，再次超越了之前的表现。
AI.summary: 本文提出并操作化了一个基于教育文献的八种沟通角色分类法，用于分析团队协作中的角色动态。研究通过标注学生Slack消息语料库，并利用LLMs进行可扩展的角色标注，揭示了团队生命周期中角色动态的变化规律。实验结果表明，该角色构建能有效预测同伴认可和团队绩效提升，且在教育和通用数据集上均表现优异，验证了其有效性和通用性。
AI.keywords: 沟通角色, 团队绩效, 角色动态, LLM标注, 同伴认可
AI.comments: 本文的创新之处在于其将理论基础的沟通角色分类法引入计算研究，并通过LLMs实现了可扩展的角色标注，为团队协作分析提供了一个新颖且可解释的视角。其发现的角色动态规律以及在预测同伴认可和团队绩效方面的卓越表现，展示了该方法在理解和优化团队协作方面的巨大潜力。同时，在不同数据集上的通用性验证也增强了研究的实际应用价值。

title: NIVA: A Multimodal Foundation Model for Actionable Earth System Intelligence
summary: Recent advances in AI-driven weather and climate modeling have improved forecast skill while reducing computational cost. However, existing data-driven approaches are limited in their ability to model coupled Earth system dynamics, which is required for extending predictability beyond the ~2-week horizon. To address this, we introduce NIVA, a multimodal foundation model designed to learn unified representations across Earth system components. While the full framework targets atmosphere, ocean, ice, and land interactions, we focus here on a two-modality setting (ocean and atmosphere) as a controlled proof of concept to evaluate whether foundation models can learn coupled dynamics. Trained on large-scale Earth system simulations, NIVA learns physically meaningful cross-modal structure, providing a foundation for subseasonal-to-seasonal prediction. As initial validation, we show that NIVA captures key modes of climate variability through accurate prediction of major climate indices.

AI.title_translation: NIVA：一个用于可操作地球系统智能的多模态基础模型
AI.tldr: NIVA是一个多模态基础模型，旨在通过学习地球系统组件的统一表示来解决现有数据驱动方法在模拟耦合地球系统动力学方面的局限性，以实现超两周的预测。初步验证显示，NIVA能捕捉关键气候变率模式并准确预测主要气候指数。
AI.motivation: 现有AI驱动的天气和气候模型在预测技能和计算成本方面有所改进，但它们在模拟耦合地球系统动力学方面的能力有限，这限制了将可预测性扩展到约两周之外。
AI.method: 引入NIVA，一个多模态基础模型，旨在学习地球系统组件的统一表示。作为概念验证，专注于双模态设置（海洋和大气），并在大规模地球系统模拟数据上进行训练，以评估基础模型是否能学习耦合动力学。
AI.result: NIVA学习了具有物理意义的跨模态结构，为次季节到季节预测奠定了基础。初步验证表明，NIVA通过准确预测主要气候指数，捕捉了气候变率的关键模式。
AI.conclusion: NIVA作为一个多模态基础模型，能够学习耦合地球系统动力学，为扩展地球系统预测的可预测性提供了基础，并能捕捉关键气候变率模式。
AI.translation: 最近人工智能驱动的天气和气候建模的进展提高了预测技能，同时降低了计算成本。然而，现有数据驱动方法在模拟耦合地球系统动力学方面的能力有限，而这对于将可预测性扩展到约两周之外是必需的。为了解决这个问题，我们引入了NIVA，一个多模态基础模型，旨在学习地球系统组件的统一表示。虽然完整的框架目标是大气、海洋、冰和陆地之间的相互作用，但我们在此专注于双模态设置（海洋和大气），作为受控的概念验证，以评估基础模型是否能学习耦合动力学。NIVA在大型地球系统模拟数据上进行训练，学习了具有物理意义的跨模态结构，为次季节到季节预测奠定了基础。作为初步验证，我们展示了NIVA通过准确预测主要气候指数，捕捉了气候变率的关键模式。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了NIVA，一个多模态基础模型，旨在解决现有AI模型在模拟耦合地球系统动力学方面的局限性，从而将预测能力扩展到两周以上。NIVA通过在海洋和大气双模态设置下，从大规模地球系统模拟数据中学习统一表示和物理意义的跨模态结构。初步结果显示NIVA能够捕捉关键气候变异模式并准确预测主要气候指数，为次季节到季节预测提供了基础。
AI.keywords: 多模态基础模型, 地球系统智能, 耦合动力学, 次季节到季节预测, 气候变率
AI.comments: NIVA通过引入多模态基础模型来解决地球系统预测中的核心挑战，即耦合动力学。其创新之处在于尝试用统一表示来整合不同地球系统组件，并为超两周的预测提供可能。尽管目前仅限于双模态验证，但其展示的潜力对于提升气候和天气预测具有重要意义。

title: Turn-Averaged SAEs for Feature Discovery and Long-Context Attribution
summary: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have become a useful tool for extracting interpretable features in language models. However, standard SAE architectures operate on individual token activations, meaning that the number of active features scales linearly with context length, and studying long model transcripts becomes difficult. We introduce turn-averaged SAEs, which represent a single Human or Assistant turn with a fixed number of features by learning to reconstruct the average model activation across the turn. We find that turn-averaged features describe a single turn's high-level characteristics more completely than per-token features when judged by an LLM. We also demonstrate that turn-averaged SAEs greatly simplify common downstream uses of SAEs like attribution graphs. Broadly, turn-averaged SAEs make interpretability techniques practical at long context lengths.

AI.title_translation: 回合平均稀疏自编码器（SAE）用于特征发现和长上下文归因
AI.tldr: 标准稀疏自编码器（SAE）在长上下文处理中存在特征数量随上下文长度线性增长的问题，导致解释性分析困难。本文引入了回合平均稀疏自编码器，通过对回合内平均模型激活进行重建，用固定数量的特征表示单个回合，从而提高了长上下文的解释性和实用性。
AI.motivation: 标准的稀疏自编码器（SAE）架构在单个token激活上操作，导致活跃特征的数量随上下文长度线性扩展，使得研究长模型转录本变得困难，限制了其在长上下文长度下的解释性应用。
AI.method: 本文引入了回合平均稀疏自编码器，通过学习重建回合的平均模型激活，用固定数量的特征来表示单个用户或助手回合。
AI.result: 研究发现，回合平均特征比逐token特征更能完整地描述单个回合的高级特性（经LLM判断）。此外，回合平均稀疏自编码器极大地简化了SAE的常见下游用途，例如归因图。
AI.conclusion: 回合平均稀疏自编码器使得可解释性技术在长上下文长度下变得实用。
AI.translation: 稀疏自编码器（SAE）已成为在语言模型中提取可解释特征的有用工具。然而，标准的SAE架构在单个token激活上操作，这意味着活跃特征的数量随上下文长度线性扩展，使得研究长模型转录本变得困难。我们引入了回合平均稀疏自编码器，它通过学习重建回合的平均模型激活，用固定数量的特征来表示单个用户或助手回合。我们发现，当由大型语言模型（LLM）判断时，回合平均特征比逐token特征更能完整地描述单个回合的高级特性。我们还证明了回合平均稀疏自编码器极大地简化了SAE的常见下游用途，例如归因图。总的来说，回合平均稀疏自编码器使得可解释性技术在长上下文长度下变得实用。
AI.summary: 本文针对标准稀疏自编码器（SAE）在长上下文处理中特征数量随上下文长度线性扩展的问题，提出了一种新的回合平均稀疏自编码器。该方法通过学习重建对话回合的平均模型激活，用固定数量的特征来表示每个回合。实验表明，回合平均特征能更完整地描述回合的高级特性，并且能显著简化SAE的下游应用，如归因图，从而使基于SAE的解释性技术在长上下文场景下变得更加实用。
AI.keywords: 稀疏自编码器, SAEs, 解释性, 长上下文, 语言模型, 回合平均
AI.comments: 这项工作的创新之处在于解决了稀疏自编码器在长上下文场景下的可扩展性问题，使得解释性技术更加实用。通过对回合内的激活进行平均，该方法提供了一种更紧凑且可能更高层次的对话动态表示，这对于理解复杂的大型语言模型行为至关重要。

title: DataComp-VLM: Improved Open Datasets for Vision-Language Models
summary: Building performant Vision-Language Models (VLMs) requires carefully curating large-scale training datasets, yet the community lacks systematic benchmarks for evaluating such curation strategies. We introduce DataComp for VLMs (DCVLM), a benchmark for controlled data-centric experiments to improve VLM training. As part of DCVLM, we collect 160 datasets spanning four data types -- image-caption pairs, multimodal interleaved documents, text-only, and instruction-tuning data -- into a corpus of 6T multimodal tokens. DCVLM allows participants to test curation strategies (filtering, mixing, formatting, sampling) across 1B-8B models and 6.25B-200B token budgets. Models are then evaluated on a carefully selected suite of up to 52 downstream benchmarks across 9 domains. We conduct extensive experiments on DCVLM and find that data mixing, not filtering, is key to a high-quality training dataset: instruction-heavy mixtures scale better than caption-heavy ones, with gains widening at larger scales. The resulting dataset, DCVLM-Baseline, enables training an 8B VLM to 63.6% accuracy on our 33-task core suite with 200B training tokens. Compared to FineVision, the state-of-the-art open VLM training dataset, this represents an improvement of +5.4pp. DCVLM and all accompanying artifacts will be made publicly available at https://www.datacomp.ai/dcvlm/.

AI.title_translation: DataComp-VLM：改进的视觉语言模型开放数据集
AI.tldr: DataComp for VLMs (DCVLM) 是一个用于评估VLM数据整理策略的基准。它收集了6T多模态token的数据集，并发现数据混合（特别是指令密集型混合）比数据过滤更关键。DCVLM-Baseline数据集使8B VLM的性能比现有技术提高了5.4pp。
AI.motivation: 构建高性能视觉语言模型（VLM）需要精心策划大规模训练数据集，但社区缺乏系统性的基准来评估这些数据整理策略。

title: Improving Coherence in Hierarchical Time Series Forecasting using Structured Temporal Fusion
comments: 7 pages, 2 figures. Preprint. Source files included
summary:
In many real-world applications, such as retail sales, energy usage, and supply chain planning, forecasting is performed across hierarchical structures. These structures often represent aggregations (e.g., products to categories to regions), where forecasts must not only be accurate but also coherent, meaning that lower-level predictions sum correctly to higher-level forecasts. Traditional statistical methods, such as Bottom-Up and MinT, enforce coherence through post-processing but fail to model complex nonlinear temporal dependencies and covariate interactions.
  We propose Hierarchical Temporal Fusion (HTF), a novel extension of the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) that integrates structured hierarchical embeddings with a coherence-aware loss function to ensure consistent forecasts across all levels of a hierarchy. Rather than applying reconciliation after forecasting, HTF embeds coherence directly into the training objective. The coherence loss penalizes the difference between aggregated child forecasts and their corresponding parent forecasts during training, enabling the model to learn both temporal dynamics and structural consistency simultaneously.
  We evaluate HTF on two publicly available benchmark datasets: the M5 Walmart forecasting dataset and a publicly available hierarchical energy consumption dataset. Results demonstrate that HTF substantially reduces forecast incoherence while improving forecasting accuracy compared with classical reconciliation methods and deep learning baselines. In addition, attention visualization and embedding analysis provide insight into how temporal and structural information contribute to hierarchical forecasting performance.

AI.title_translation: 使用结构化时间融合改进分层时间序列预测中的连贯性
AI.tldr: 提出HTF模型，通过集成结构化分层嵌入和连贯性感知损失函数，在分层时间序列预测中同时提高准确性和连贯性，优于传统方法和深度学习基线。
AI.motivation: 在零售销售、能源使用和供应链规划等许多实际应用中，预测在分层结构中进行。这些结构通常代表聚合，其中预测不仅必须准确，而且必须连贯，这意味着较低级别的预测必须正确地汇总到较高级别的预测。传统的统计方法通过后处理强制执行连贯性，但未能模拟复杂的非线性时间依赖性和协变量交互。
AI.method: 提出分层时间融合（HTF），它是时间融合转换器（TFT）的一个新颖扩展，它将结构化分层嵌入与连贯性感知损失函数相结合，以确保层次结构所有级别的预测一致。HTF不是在预测后应用协调，而是将连贯性直接嵌入到训练目标中。连贯性损失在训练期间惩罚聚合子预测与其相应父预测之间的差异，使模型能够同时学习时间动态和结构一致性。
AI.result: 在M5 Walmart预测数据集和公共分层能源消耗数据集上进行评估。结果表明，与经典协调方法和深度学习基线相比，HTF显著降低了预测不连贯性，同时提高了预测准确性。此外，注意力可视化和嵌入分析提供了关于时间信息和结构信息如何促进分层预测性能的见解。
AI.conclusion: HTF通过在训练中直接整合连贯性，在分层时间序列预测中实现了更高的准确性和连贯性，优于现有方法。
AI.translation:
在许多现实世界的应用中，例如零售销售、能源使用和供应链规划，预测是在分层结构中进行的。这些结构通常代表聚合（例如，产品到类别到区域），其中预测不仅必须准确，而且必须连贯，这意味着较低级别的预测必须正确地汇总到较高级别的预测。传统的统计方法，例如自下而上和MinT，通过后处理强制执行连贯性，但未能模拟复杂的非线性时间依赖性和协变量交互。
我们提出了分层时间融合（HTF），它是时间融合转换器（TFT）的一个新颖扩展，它将结构化分层嵌入与连贯性感知损失函数相结合，以确保层次结构所有级别的预测一致。HTF不是在预测后应用协调，而是将连贯性直接嵌入到训练目标中。连贯性损失在训练期间惩罚聚合子预测与其相应父预测之间的差异，使模型能够同时学习时间动态和结构一致性。
我们在两个公开可用的基准数据集上评估了HTF：M5 Walmart预测数据集和一个公开可用的分层能源消耗数据集。结果表明，与经典协调方法和深度学习基线相比，HTF显著降低了预测不连贯性，同时提高了预测准确性。此外，注意力可视化和嵌入分析提供了关于时间信息和结构信息如何促进分层预测性能的见解。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种名为分层时间融合（HTF）的新型模型，旨在解决分层时间序列预测中的连贯性与准确性问题。HTF是时间融合转换器（TFT）的扩展，通过集成结构化分层嵌入和连贯性感知损失函数，在训练阶段直接确保预测的结构一致性，而非通过后处理。实验结果表明，HTF在减少预测不连贯性和提高预测准确性方面优于传统协调方法和深度学习基线，并在M5 Walmart和能源消耗数据集上得到了验证。
AI.keywords: 分层时间序列预测, 连贯性, 时间融合转换器, 深度学习, 结构化嵌入
AI.comments: 该论文的创新点在于将连贯性约束直接整合到深度学习模型的训练目标中，而不是依赖于后处理。这种方法使得模型能够同时学习时间动态和结构一致性，从而在分层时间序列预测中实现了显著的性能提升。这对于需要高精度和结构一致性预测的实际应用（如零售和能源管理）具有重要意义。

title: Robotic Arm-Based Spectral Sensing for Strawberry Positioning and Non-Destructive Sweetness Measurement
summary:
Accurate assessment of sweetness is essential for quality control in agriculture, yet conventional methods rely on destructive sampling and are difficult to scale. This thesis presents a robotic arm-based spectral sensing system for strawberry detection, localization, approach, and non-destructive sweetness estimation.
  The system integrates perception, calibration, and robotic control in a closed-loop pipeline. A YOLOv11s detector is adopted for real-time strawberry detection, while RGB-ToF calibration and mask-to-depth alignment are used to obtain geometrically consistent target localization. A custom eye-in-hand hand-eye calibration workflow is developed to estimate the rigid transform between gripper_link and cam_front, enabling reliable transformation of fruit targets into the robot base frame. Based on these estimates, the robot executes a waypoint-based search and an incremental closed-loop approach strategy to position the sensor at optimal working distance for sweetness sensing.
  Experimental results show strong end-to-end performance (88.10% success over 42 trials), with robust detection (95.24%) and successful approach execution once a target is detected (100% conditional success). Hand-eye calibration comparisons indicate that although Andreff yields the smallest translation norm in single-run results, the Park method provides better cross-sample consistency and therefore more stable downstream robot behavior. The residual failures are concentrated in the sensing stage, especially valid-region extraction for sweetness estimation under difficult depth/reflectance conditions.
  Overall, this work demonstrates the feasibility of integrating RGB-ToF perception, robotic manipulation, and non-destructive sensing for practical strawberry quality assessment, and provides a scalable baseline for future integration of learning-based policies such as Vision-Language-Action models.

AI.title_translation: 基于机械臂的光谱传感器的草莓定位与无损甜度测量
AI.tldr: 该论文提出了一种基于机械臂的光谱传感系统，用于草莓的检测、定位、接近和无损甜度估测，实现了88.10%的端到端成功率，并为未来集成学习策略提供了基础。
AI.motivation: 传统的草莓甜度测量方法依赖于破坏性采样且难以规模化，因此需要一种能够进行无损、大规模草莓甜度评估的方法。
AI.method: 该系统集成了感知、标定和机器人控制，采用YOLOv11s进行草莓检测，RGB-ToF标定和掩码到深度对齐以获得目标定位，并开发了自定义的眼中手标定工作流来估计机器人坐标系下的目标位置，最后通过基于航点搜索和增量式闭环接近策略来优化传感器工作距离，以进行甜度传感。
AI.result: 实验结果显示，端到端成功率为88.10%（42次试验），其中草莓检测成功率为95.24%，检测到目标后的接近执行成功率为100%。Park方法在手眼标定方面比Andreff方法具有更好的跨样本一致性。传感阶段的失败主要集中在提取用于甜度估测的有效区域，特别是在具有挑战性的深度/反射条件下。
AI.conclusion: 该研究证明了集成RGB-ToF感知、机器人操作和无损传感技术在实际草莓品质评估中的可行性，并为未来集成基于学习的策略（如Vision-Language-Action模型）提供了可扩展的基础。
AI.translation:
准确评估甜度对于农业质量控制至关重要，但传统方法依赖于破坏性采样且难以规模化。本论文提出了一种基于机械臂的光谱传感系统，用于草莓的检测、定位、接近和无损甜度估测。
该系统在闭环流程中集成了感知、标定和机器人控制。采用YOLOv11s检测器进行实时草莓检测，而RGB-ToF标定和掩码到深度对齐用于获得几何上一致的目标定位。开发了自定义的眼中有手标定工作流，以估算夹持器连杆和前置摄像头之间的刚性变换，从而能够将水果目标可靠地转换到机器人基坐标系。基于这些估算，机器人执行基于航点的搜索和增量式的闭环接近策略，以将传感器定位在最佳工作距离以进行甜度传感。
实验结果表明，端到端性能（42次试验的成功率为88.10%）表现强劲，检测鲁棒性（95.24%），一旦检测到目标，接近执行成功（条件成功率为100%）。手眼标定比较表明，虽然Andreff在单次运行结果中具有最小的平移范数，但Park方法提供了更好的跨样本一致性，因此具有更稳定的下游机器人行为。剩余的失败集中在传感阶段，特别是在困难的深度/反射条件下进行甜度估测的有效区域提取。
总的来说，这项工作证明了集成RGB-ToF感知、机器人操作和无损传感技术在实际草莓品质评估中的可行性，并为未来集成基于学习的策略，如Vision-Language-Action模型，提供了一个可扩展的基础。
AI.summary: 本研究开发了一个集成RGB-ToF感知、机器人控制和光谱传感的系统，用于草莓的无损甜度测量。通过YOLOv11s检测、精确的几何标定和优化的机器人接近策略，系统实现了高效的草莓定位和甜度估测。实验结果显示了该系统在端到端成功率、检测和接近方面的鲁棒性，并为未来在农业质量控制中应用先进的机器人和AI技术奠定了基础。
AI.keywords: 草莓甜度测量, 无损传感, 机器人抓取, 光谱传感, 计算机视觉
AI.comments: 该研究在草莓无损甜度测量方面取得了显著进展，通过集成多种先进技术（如RGB-ToF、YOLOv11s、眼中有手标定和机器人闭环控制），实现了较高的成功率。然而，在传感阶段，特别是在处理复杂深度/反射条件下的有效区域提取方面仍存在挑战，这为未来的研究提供了方向。该研究的另一个亮点是为集成更复杂的学习策略（如Vision-Language-Action模型）提供了可扩展的基础，这预示着未来农业自动化和智能化水平的提升。

title: IMCBench: A benchmark for multimodal LLMs in Image-grounded Medical Conversations
comments: Accepted at ECML PKDD 2026. 22 pages, 2 figures
summary: Recent advances in large language models and vision-language models have enabled reasoning over multimodal data, offering opportunities for clinical applications such as decision support and triaging. However, existing medical AI benchmarks are fragmented: some support multi-turn dialogues but lack images, while others provide multimodal inputs but focus on single-turn QA tasks. To address this gap, we introduce IMCBench, an image-grounded, multi-turn medical conversation benchmark that pairs real, publicly available clinical images with synthetic patient profiles to simulate realistic patient-clinician interactions. Each conversation is evaluated across three clinical dimensions: safety, accuracy, and appropriate use of uncertainty in diagnosis. We benchmark eight multimodal frontier models across four model families (Claude, GPT, Nova, and Llama), scoring each on a 1-5 scale using LLM-as-Jury scoring calibrated against expert clinician annotations. Our results show that Claude Opus 4.6 achieves the highest overall score (3.61), followed by Claude Sonnet 4.6 (3.30) and GPT-5.2 (3.29), though no model dominates all dimensions and safety degrades for both malignant and rare conditions ($Δ$ = -0.27 each). Ablation studies further reveal that both visual input and EHR context contribute to safe guidance (safety drops of 0.18 and 0.23 on average when each is removed), with stronger models leveraging visual features more effectively. Together, these findings demonstrate that accurate clinical description does not guarantee safe patient guidance, motivating the need for multi-dimensional evaluation frameworks in medical AI.
